high.title: Ringgit strengthens against major regional currencies
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0680 against the US dollar, strengthening across major currencies as US-Iran peace negotiations progressed and crude oil prices stabilized. Key US economic data releases this week, including nonfarm payrolls and consumer confidence indices, will be critical in determining future USD strength and ringgit performance. Malaysian investors and importers/exporters should monitor these developments closely.

high.title: Bursa pares earlier losses to end slightly lower
high.summary: The FBM KLCI ended slightly lower amid mixed regional sentiment driven by Middle East geopolitical risks, AI valuation concerns, and China's new export controls on Japanese companies. However, bargain hunting in the afternoon session lifted mid- and small-cap indices, with FBM 70 and FBM Small Cap closing higher. The KLCI is approaching oversold levels, which may signal selective accumulation opportunities for investors.

high.title: Stocks adrift, oil up as US-Iran halt renewed attacks
high.summary: Global markets remained directionless as US-Iran ceasefire uncertainty pushed Brent crude up 0.85% to US$72.6 per barrel, affecting energy costs and inflation globally. Asian markets were broadly negative, with South Korea's KOSPI falling nearly 2% and Japan's Nikkei slipping 1%, weighing on regional sentiment including Malaysia. Rising oil prices and geopolitical instability in the Middle East have direct implications for Malaysia's energy sector and trade.

high.title: Ringgit Extends Gains Against US Dollar, Regional Peers
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar amid softer Fed rate hike expectations following mixed US economic data, including Q1 2026 GDP growth of 2.1% and weak consumer spending of only 0.5%. Lower US yields are easing pressure on Asian currencies including the ringgit. Malaysian investors should monitor USD/MYR movements as these macroeconomic shifts impact trade, corporate earnings, and capital flows.

high.title: Banking Stocks Lift Bursa at Close
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 0.24% at 1,667.75, supported by a late rebound in banking stocks and continued strength in telecommunications counters. Market sentiment remained cautious amid global volatility tied to uncertainty in the AI investment theme. This reflects broader investor hesitancy that could influence near-term equity positioning in Malaysia.

high.title: Ringgit opens lower as strong US GDP lifts dollar
high.summary: The ringgit weakened to 4.1170/4.1270 against the USD as stronger-than-expected US Q1 GDP of 2.1% boosted the dollar. However, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz improved risk appetite, limiting further ringgit decline. PCE inflation data in line with expectations may temper the dollar's rally.

high.title: Ringgit continues stellar performance, ends higher for third consecutive day
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.1160/4.1200 against the greenback, marking its third consecutive day of gains. Declining crude oil prices and expectations of easing US inflation are key drivers, with Brent crude falling 38.3% from its April peak. Upcoming PCE data remains a critical factor for near-term monetary policy direction.

high.title: Selling pressure drags Bursa lower
high.summary: The FBM KLCI fell 1.09% or 18.31 points to close at 1,663.82, driven by broad-based weakness in industrial and banking heavyweights. Banking stocks faced sustained pressure as hawkish signals from the ECB, Bank of Japan, and US Fed reinforced a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. Cautious investor sentiment ahead of the US PCE data release further weighed on the market.

high.title: Ringgit opens firmer on stronger investor sentiment, FDI surge
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar at market open, supported by a significant surge in Malaysia's FDI to RM65.9 billion in 2025 from RM46.7 billion in 2024. Malaysia's cumulative FDI position rose to RM1.09 trillion, equivalent to 53.7% of GDP, signalling strong foreign investor confidence. Additionally, declining crude oil prices linked to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz adds a key macroeconomic variable for energy-related investments.

medium.title: Bursa retreats at open as sentiment turns cautious
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI fell 5.70 points to 1,662.04 at the open as Wall Street weakness in tech stocks and escalating US-Iran tensions dampened sentiment. Analysts recommend cautious accumulation, with the index expected to trade in the 1,665-1,675 range. The cautious undertone reflects broader global uncertainty that Malaysian equity investors should factor into short-term positioning.

medium.title: Spain raises 2026 growth forecast despite Middle East war turmoil
medium.summary: Spain revised its 2026 GDP growth forecast upward, demonstrating economic resilience despite global energy market volatility caused by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The ongoing Middle East conflict and its inflationary impact on global energy markets serve as a key external risk factor relevant to Malaysian trade and inflation dynamics. This signals that some economies can weather geopolitical shocks, offering context for assessing Malaysia's own economic resilience.

medium.title: Ringgit Slightly Higher Against Greenback, Supported by Low Oil Prices
medium.summary: The ringgit opened slightly higher at 4.0855/4.0950 against the US dollar, supported by subdued oil prices and easing geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts expect the USD/MYR pair to trade between RM4.08 and RM4.10. Oil price stability is a key factor for Malaysia's export revenues and currency outlook.

medium.title: Six-Month Extension for Stamp Duty Disclosure Programme
medium.summary: LHDN has extended the voluntary stamp duty disclosure programme to encourage compliance as Malaysia transitions to a self-assessment system for stamp duty. Instruments executed between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2025 are eligible for automatic penalty waivers upon payment, with no separate appeal required. Businesses and property owners with outstanding stamp duty obligations should act before the December 31, 2026 deadline.

medium.title: Bursa Opens Slightly Higher on Bargain Hunting
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened marginally higher with the FBM KLCI rising 1.82 points to 1,665.64, driven by bargain hunting despite negative market breadth. Wall Street's mixed close, weighed down by AI stock volatility and Apple's price hikes, tempered local sentiment. The cautious tone suggests investors are selectively positioning amid global uncertainty.

medium.title: Thailand, Argentina primed as next supply chain rising stars
medium.summary: A Verisk Maplecroft report highlights Thailand and other Southeast Asian nations as emerging supply chain beneficiaries as companies diversify beyond cost efficiency to build resilience. The temporary shuttering of the Strait of Hormuz created near-term headwinds but longer-term opportunities remain attractive. This has indirect implications for Malaysia as it competes for supply chain investment in the region.

medium.title: Bursa opens higher, extends gains on bargain hunting
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened 2.32 points higher at 1,684.45, supported by bargain hunting with gainers outnumbering decliners at the open. Wall Street's mixed close, with gains in industrials offset by declines in oil and gas and telecoms, provided a cautious backdrop. Early positive breadth suggested selective investor interest despite broader market uncertainties.
